enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: Indicates to the transmit data FIFO that the written frames contain two additional octets before the frame data. This means the actual frame begins at bit 16 of the first word written into the FIFO. This function allows putting the frame payload on a 32-bit boundary in memory, as the 14-byte Ethernet header is extended to a 16-byte header.

field.name: IPCHK
field.description: Enables insertion of IP header checksum.

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: If an IP frame is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically. The IP header checksum field must be cleared. If a non-IP frame is transmitted the frame is not modified.

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: If an IP frame with a known protocol is transmitted, the checksum is inserted automatically into the frame. The checksum field must be cleared. The other frames are not modified.

field.name: PADREM
field.description: Enable Padding Removal For Short IP Frames

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: Any bytes following the IP payload section of the frame are removed from the frame.

field.name: IPDIS
field.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong IPv4 Header Checksum

enumeratedValue.name: ZERO
enumeratedValue.description: Frames with wrong IPv4 header checksum are not discarded.

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: If an IPv4 frame is received with a mismatching header checksum, the frame is discarded. IPv6 has no header checksum and is not affected by this setting. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).

field.name: PRODIS
field.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With Wrong Protocol Checksum

enumeratedValue.name: ZERO
enumeratedValue.description: Frames with wrong checksum are not discarded.

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: If a TCP/IP, UDP/IP, or ICMP/IP frame is received that has a wrong TCP, UDP, or ICMP checksum, the frame is discarded. Discarding is only available when the RX FIFO operates in store and forward mode (RSFL cleared).

field.name: LINEDIS
field.description: Enable Discard Of Frames With MAC Layer Errors

enumeratedValue.name: ZERO
enumeratedValue.description: Frames with errors are not discarded.

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: Any frame received with a CRC, length, or PHY error is automatically discarded and not forwarded to the user application interface.

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: Instructs the MAC to write two additional bytes in front of each frame received into the RX FIFO.

enumeratedValue.name: ZERO

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: The timer can be reset to zero when the given offset time is reached (offset event). The field is cleared when the offset event is reached, so no further event occurs until the field is set again. The timer offset value must be set before setting this field.

enumeratedValue.name: ONE

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: A period event interrupt can be generated (EIR[TS_TIMER]) and the event signal output is asserted when the timer wraps around according to the periodic setting ATPER. The timer period value must be set before setting this bit. Not all devices contain the event signal output. See the chip configuration details.

enumeratedValue.name: ONE
enumeratedValue.description: The internal timer is disabled and the externally provided timer value is used. All other fields, except CAPTURE, in this register have no effect. CAPTURE can still be used to capture the current timer value.

enumeratedValue.name: DUAL_COUNTER
enumeratedValue.description: Dual counter. The SCT operates as two 16-bit counters named COUNTER_L and COUNTER_H.

enumeratedValue.name: UNIFIED_COUNTER
enumeratedValue.description: Unified counter. The SCT operates as a unified 32-bit counter.

enumeratedValue.name: SYSTEM_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: System Clock Mode. The system clock clocks the entire SCT module including all counters and counter prescalers.

enumeratedValue.name: SAMPLED_SYSTEM_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Sampled System Clock Mode. The system clock clocks the SCT module, but the counter and prescalers are only enabled to count when the designated edge is detected on the input selected by the CKSEL field. The minimum pulse width on the selected clock-gate input is 1 bus clock period. This mode is the high-performance, sampled-clock mode.

enumeratedValue.name: SCT_INPUT_CLOCK_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: SCT Input Clock Mode. The input/edge selected by the CKSEL field clocks the SCT module, including all counters and prescalers, after first being synchronized to the system clock. The minimum pulse width on the clock input is 1 bus clock period. This mode is the low-power, sampled-clock mode.

enumeratedValue.name: ASYNCHRONOUS_MODE
enumeratedValue.description: Asynchronous Mode. The entire SCT module is clocked directly by the input/edge selected by the CKSEL field. In this mode, the SCT outputs are switched synchronously to the SCT input clock - not the system clock. The input clock rate must be at least half the system clock rate and can be the same or faster than the system clock.

field.name: CKSEL
field.description: SCT Clock Select. The specific functionality of the designated input/edge is dependent on the CLKMODE bit selection in this register.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_RELOAD
enumeratedValue.description: No Reload. Prevents the lower match registers from being reloaded from their respective reload registers.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_RELOAD_H
enumeratedValue.description: No Reload. Prevents the higher match registers from being reloaded from their respective reload registers.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. A match on match register 0 is the LIMIT condition. No need to define an associated event.

enumeratedValue.name: ENABLE
enumeratedValue.description: Enable. A match on match register 0 is the LIMIT condition. No need to define an associated event.

enumeratedValue.name: DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Down. The L or unified counter is counting down.

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Up. The counter counts up to a limit condition, then is cleared to zero.

enumeratedValue.name: UP_DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Up-down. The counter counts up to a limit, then counts down to a limit condition or to 0.

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Up. The H counter is counting up.

enumeratedValue.name: DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Down. The H counter is counting down.

enumeratedValue.name: UP
enumeratedValue.description: Up. The H counter counts up to its limit condition, then is cleared to zero.

enumeratedValue.name: UP_DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Up-down. The H counter counts up to its limit, then counts down to a limit condition or to 0.

field.name: STARTMSK_L
field.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the CTRL[STOP_L] = 0 (event 0 = bit 0, event 1 = bit 1, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

field.name: STARTMSK_H
field.description: If bit n is one, event n clears the CTRL[STOP_H] = 0 (event 0 = bit 16, event 1 = bit 17, etc.). The number of bits = number of events in this SCT.

enumeratedValue.description: IO. Uses the specified I/O condition only.

enumeratedValue.name: AND
enumeratedValue.description: AND. The event occurs when the specified match and I/O condition occur simultaneously.

enumeratedValue.name: ADD
enumeratedValue.description: Add. STATEV value is added into STATE (the carry-out is ignored).

enumeratedValue.name: LOAD
enumeratedValue.description: Load. STATEV value is loaded into STATE.

enumeratedValue.name: DIRECTION_INDEPENDENT
enumeratedValue.description: Direction independent. This event is triggered regardless of the count direction.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTING_UP
enumeratedValue.description: Counting up. This event is triggered only during up-counting when BIDIR = 1.

enumeratedValue.name: COUNTING_DOWN
enumeratedValue.description: Counting down. This event is triggered only during down-counting when BIDIR = 1.

field.name: CCCR_REV
field.description: CCCR Format Version Number Version of the CCCR format that this card supports.

field.name: SDIO_REV
field.description: SDIO Specification Revision Number Version of the SDIO specification that this card supports.

field.name: SD_PHY_REV
field.description: SD Format Version Number Version of the SD Physical specification that this card supports.

field.name: IOE
field.description: Function I/O enable 0 = function disabled 1 = function enabled

field.name: FN_IO_RDY
field.description: Function I/O ready 0 = function not ready to operate 1 = function ready to operate

field.name: HOST_IEN
field.description: Host Interrupt Enable 0 = no interrupts from this card sent to host 1 = any function's interrupt sent to host

field.name: IEN
field.description: Function Interrupt Enable 0 = interrupt from this function not sent to host 1 = interrupt from this function sent to host (host_ien must also be set)

field.name: FN_INT_HOST
field.description: Function Interrupt Pending 0 = no interrupts pending from this function 1 = interrupt pending If the ien[x] or host_ien bits are not set in INT_ENABLE, the host will not receive the pending interrupt.

field.name: ABORT_SEL
field.description: Abort Select To abort an I/O read or write to free the SD bus, the function that is currently transferring data must be addressed.

field.name: IO_CARD_RST
field.description: I/O Card Reset If host sets this bit, an interrupt is generated to the card.

field.name: BUS_WIDTH
field.description: Bus Width Data bus width used for data transfer 00 = 1 bit 10 = 4 bits All full-speed SDIO cards support both 1-bit and 4-bit bus.

field.name: SCSI
field.description: Support continuous SPI Interrupt writable from internal bus only 0 = SPI supports interrupt assertion only when CS (SD)DAT[3] pin) is asserted 1 = SPI supports interrupt assertion independent of CS

field.name: CD_DISABLE
field.description: Connect/Disconnet Disable Connect[0]/disconnect[1] the 10K-90 kO pull-up resistor on pin 1 of card.

field.name: SDC
field.description: Support Direct Commands Card supports direct commands during multi-byte transfer 0 = all I/O functions do not accept and execute 1 = all I/O functions accept and execute

field.name: SMB
field.description: Support Multi-Block Card supports multi block indicator 0 = all I/O functions do not accept and execute 1 = all I/O functions accept and execute

field.name: S4MI
field.description: Support 4-bit Mode Interrupt Supports interrupt between blocks of data in 4-bit mode 0 = card not able to signal an interrupt during a 4-bit multi-block data transfer 1 = card is able to signal an interrupt between blocks during data transfer

field.name: E4MI
field.description: Enable 4-bit Mode Interrupt Enable interrupt between blocks of data in 4-bit mode.

field.name: BUS_STATUS
field.description: Bus Status Bus status indicator 0 = N/A 1 = currently addressed function is currently executing a command

field.name: BUS_RELEASE
field.description: Bus Release Bus release request/status indicator 0 = N/A 1 = suspend request still in progress

field.name: FN0_BLK_SIZE0
field.description: Block size [7:0] for Function 0 I/O block operations

field.name: FN0_BLK_SIZE1
field.description: Block size [8] for Function 0 I/O block operations

field.name: SMPC
field.description: Support Master Power Control 0 = do not support 1 = support

field.name: EMPC
field.description: Enable Master Power Control 0 = disable 1 = enable

field.name: SHS
field.description: Support High Speed Mode 0 = do not support 1 = support

field.name: BSS
field.description: Select Ultra High Speed Mode BSS Bus speed(1.

field.name: SSDR50
field.description: This bit indicates support of sdr50.

field.name: SSDR104
field.description: This bit indicates support of sdr104.

field.name: SDDR50
field.description: This bit indicates support of ddr50.

field.name: SDTA
field.description: Support Driver Type A This bit indicates support of Driver Type A

field.name: SDTC
field.description: Support Driver Type C This bit indicates support of Driver Type C

field.name: SDTD
field.description: Support Driver Type D This bit indicates support of Driver Type D

field.name: SAI
field.description: Support Asynchronous Interrupt Support bit of asynchronous interrupt.

field.name: EAI
field.description: Enable Asynchronous Interrupt Enable bit of asynchronous interrupt.

field.name: CMD52_WR_ERR_WKUP_EN
field.description: CMD52 Write Error Wakeup Enable If host issues CMD52 write access to any off-domain register during sleep mode, setting this bit will trigger wakeup event to the APU.

field.name: CMD52_RD_ERR_WKUP_EN
field.description: CMD52 Read Error Wakeup Enable If host issues CMD52 read access to any off-domain register during sleep mode, setting this bit will trigger wakeup event to the APU.

field.name: CMD53_WR_ERR_WKUP_EN
field.description: CMD53 Write Error Wakeup Enable If host issues CMD53 write access during sleep mode, setting this bit will trigger wakeup event to the APU.

field.name: CMD53_RD_ERR_WKUP_EN
field.description: CMD53 Read Error Wakeup Enable If host issues CMD53 read access during sleep mode, setting this bit will trigger wakeup event to the APU.

field.name: SD_HOST_INT_ACT_LVL
field.description: SD Host Interrupt Active Level 0 = Active Low 1 = Active High

field.name: CMD53_RFIFO_TH
field.description: CMD53 read fifo threshold 00 = 1 block size 01 = .5 block size 10 = block size 11 = block size

field.name: NGFF_SD_RST_EN
field.description: Allow NGFF SDIO RESET# to reset OCR value.

field.name: CMD52_WR_RESP_EN
field.description: Enable delay of CMD52 write response (Not used)

field.name: CMD52_DLY_RES_RDATA_EN
field.description: Delay latching of CMD52 read data until it is serially shifted out

field.name: CMD52_PWUP_EN
field.description: If this is set to 1, host can issue any CMD52 to wake up the chip.

field.name: APU_DEV_SLEEP_EN
field.description: If this is set to 1, the IO_READY status and Card Ready status depend on APU sleep/wake state.

field.name: CMD19_TP_ADDR
field.description: CMD19 tuning pattern address Set address value for CMD19 tuning pattern array

field.name: CMD19_TP_DATA
field.description: CMD19 tuning pattern data CMD19 tuning pattern data at cmd19_tp_addr

field.name: FN_CARD_INT1
field.description: Pending card interrupt for each function to cpu1

field.name: FN_CARD_INT2
field.description: Pending card interrupt for each function to cpu2

field.name: FN_CARD_INT3
field.description: Pending card interrupt for each function to cpu3

field.name: DEV_SLEEP
field.description: Device Sleep If this is set to 1, IO_READY and CARD_READY status will be 0.

field.name: CMD53_WR_BUSY_HW_EN
field.description: Main enable bit for cmd53_wr_busy_hw_ctrl feature.

field.name: FN0_CARD_INTRSR0
field.description: Function 0 card interrupt reset select [7:0] 0 = ISR bit clears when 0 is written to it 1 = ISR bit clears when read

field.name: FN0_CARD_INTRSR1
field.description: Function 0 card interrupt reset select [15:8] 0 = ISR bit clears when 0 is written to it 1 = ISR bit clears when read

field.name: FN0_CARD_INTSTAT0
field.description: Function 0 card interrupt status [7:0] of the following events: [7:1] = fn_ps_event [0] = drv_snth_event

field.name: FN0_CARD_INTSTAT1
field.description: Function 0 card interrupt status [15:8] of the following events: [7] = FN0 CMD53 read access during sleep mode [6] = FN0 CMD53 write access during sleep mode [5] = FN0 CMD52 read access to off-domain sdu register during sleep mode [4] = FN0 CMD52 write access to off-domain sdu register during sleep mode [3] = CMD5 is received [2] = CMD11 start [1] = CMD11 switch start [0] = CMD11 succeeded

field.name: CMD11_V18_BYPASS_VAL
field.description: FW bypass value that overrides the V18 signal from the SD pad voltage sensor.

field.name: CMD11_V18_BYPASS_EN
field.description: If this is set, the V18 signal from the SD pad voltage sensor is bypassed.

field.name: CMD11_VIO_CHK_BYPASS
field.description: If this is set, the cmd11 state machine will bypass the VIO pad sensor check.

field.name: CMD11_SD_CLK_STOP_BYPASS
field.description: If this is set, the cmd11 state machine will bypass the SD clk idle checking logic.

field.name: CMD5_R4_S18A_BYPASS_VAL
field.description: FW bypass value that overrides the S18A field in cmd5 R4 response.

field.name: CMD5_R4_S18A_BYPASS_EN
field.description: If this is set, the S18A field in cmd5 R4 response is bypassed.

field.name: SET_CMD11_ILLEGAL
field.description: If this is set and SD VIO pad sensor V18=1 (1.

field.name: CMD5_S18R_CHK
field.description: If this is set, S18A in R4 depends on CMD5 S18R bit.

field.name: CMD5_R4_FN_BYPASS_VAL
field.description: FW bypass value that overrides the function number derived from chip strap settings.

field.name: CMD5_R4_FN_BYPASS_EN
field.description: If this is set, the function number field of R4 is controlled by cmd5_r4_fn_bypass_val rather than from chip strap settings.

field.name: REPEAT_SDU_INIT
field.description: If this is set, sdu can handle enumeration sequence initiated by host multiple times

field.name: SD_RESET_AFTER_CMD52_R5
field.description: Generate sd_reset after cmd52 R5 response.

field.name: CMD52_RES_VALID_MODE
field.description: CMD52 response valid mode 0 = CMD52 response valid is generated only after write operation is completed in the ahb_clk domain.

field.name: CSA
field.description: Function supports Code Storage Area (CSA) 0 = function does not support CSA 1 = function supports CSA

field.name: FN_EXT_CODE
field.description: Extended SDIO standard function interface code.

field.name: SPS
field.description: Power Selection 0 = no power selection 1 = two power modes selected by EPS bit

field.name: EPS
field.description: Current Mode 0 = function operates in high current mode 1 = function operates in low current mode

field.name: FN_CIS_PTR0
field.description: 24b Function Pointer [7:0] Function card information structure pointer [7:0] Function n CIS pointer is (0x8000 | n << 7) Therefore, Function 1 CIS pointer is 0x008080 Function 2 CIS pointer is 0x008100 Function 3 CIS pointer is 0x008180 ... Function 7 CIS pointer is 0x008380

field.name: FN_CIS_PTR1
field.description: 24b Function 1 Pointer [15:8] Function card information structure pointer [15:8]

field.name: FN_CIS_PTR2
field.description: 24b Function 1 Pointer [23:16] Function card information structure pointer [23:16]

field.name: FN_BLK_SIZE0
field.description: Block Size [7:0] for I/O Block Operation

field.name: FN_BLK_SIZE1
field.description: Block Size [8] for I/O Block Operation

field.name: HOST_PWR_DOWN
field.description: Host power down event When host sets this bit, interrupt is generated to the CPU.

field.name: HOST_PWR_UP
field.description: Host power up event When host sets this bit, interrupt is generated to the CPU.

field.name: HOST_TERMINATE_CMD53
field.description: Host terminates CMD53 When host sets this bit, current cmd53 data transfer will terminate.

field.name: HOST_TO_CARD_EVENT
field.description: Host to card event When host sets this bit, interrupt is generated to the CPU.

field.name: HOST_RST_EVENT
field.description: Host reset event When host sets this bit, interrupt is generated to the CPU.

field.name: HOST_INT_RSR0
field.description: Host Interrupt Reset Select [7:0] 0 = ISR bit clears when 0 is written to it 1 = ISR bit clears when read

field.name: HOST_INT_RSR1
field.description: Host Interrupt Reset Select [15:8] 0 = ISR bit clears when 0 is written to it 1 = ISR bit clears when read

field.name: HOST_INT_MASK0
field.description: Host Interrupt Mask [7:0] 0 = disable card to host interrupt 1 = enable card to host interrupt

field.name: HOST_INT_MASK1
field.description: Host Interrupt Mask [15:8] 0 = disable card to host interrupt 1 = enable card to host interrupt

field.name: Q0_UPLD_HOST_INT
field.description: Queue 0 Upload Host Interrupt Status Set when card has packet ready for upload and card is in I/O ready state.

field.name: Q0_DNLD_HOST_INT
field.description: Queue 0 Download Host Interrupt Status Set when card is ready for download from host.

field.name: FIFO_UNDERFLOW
field.description: Fifo Underflow Set when FIFO underflow occurs during upload.

field.name: FIFO_OVERFLOW
field.description: Fifo Overflow Set when FIFO overflow occurs during download.

field.name: CMD_PORT_UPLD_INT
field.description: Command Port Upload Host Interrupt Status Set when card has packet ready for command port upload and card is in I/O ready state.

field.name: CMD_PORT_DNLD_INT
field.description: Command Port Download Host Interrupt Status Set when card is ready for command port download from host.

field.name: Q1_UPLD_HOST_INT
field.description: Queue 1 Upload Host Interrupt Status Set when card has packet ready for upload and card is in I/O ready state.

field.name: Q2_UPLD_HOST_INT
field.description: Queue 2 Upload Host Interrupt Status Set when card has packet ready for upload and card is in I/O ready state.

field.name: Q3_UPLD_HOST_INT
field.description: Queue 3 Upload Host Interrupt Status Set when card has packet ready for upload and card is in I/O ready state.

field.name: Q1_DNLD_HOST_INT
field.description: Queue 1 Download Host Interrupt Status Set when card is ready for download from host.

field.name: Q2_DNLD_HOST_INT
field.description: Queue 2 Download Host Interrupt Status Set when card is ready for download from host.

field.name: Q3_DNLD_HOST_INT
field.description: Queue 3 Download Host Interrupt Status Set when card is ready for download from host.

field.name: DNLD_RESTART
field.description: Download Restart Host sets this bit for the card to retransmit packet.

field.name: UPLD_RESTART
field.description: Upload Restart Host sets this bit for the card to retransmit packet.

field.name: DNLD_CRC_ERR
field.description: Download Cyclic Redundancy Check Error This bit is set by HW if there is a data CRC error after a data block is downloaded.

field.name: Q0_PRT_RANGE
field.description: Queue 0 Port Range Number of ports assigned per queue.

field.name: Q1_PRT_RANGE
field.description: Queue 1 Port Range Number of ports assigned per queue.

field.name: Q2_PRT_RANGE
field.description: Queue 2 Port Range Number of ports assigned per queue.

field.name: Q3_PRT_RANGE
field.description: Queue 3 Port Range Number of ports assigned per queue.

field.name: Q0_DNLD_CARD_RDY
field.description: Queue 0 Download Card Ready Firmware sets this bit when one packet is ready.

field.name: Q0_UPLD_CARD_RDY
field.description: Queue 0 Upload Card Ready Firmware sets this bit when one packet is ready.

field.name: CIS_CARD_RDY
field.description: Card Information Structure Card Ready Firmware sets this bit after CIS table is initialized

field.name: IO_READY
field.description: I/O Ready Indicator SD target device accepts CMD53 only after the previous CMD53 has finished.

field.name: CARD_INT_MASK0
field.description: Host to Card Interrupt Mask[7:0] 0 = disable host to card interrupt 1 = enable host to card interrupt

field.name: CARD_INT_MASK1
field.description: Host to Card Interrupt Mask[15:8] 0 = disable host to card interrupt 1 = enable host to card interrupt

field.name: CARD_INT_MASK2
field.description: Host to Card Interrupt Mask [23:16] 0 = disable host to card interrupt 1 = enable host to card interrupt

field.name: ABORT_CARD_INT
field.description: Abort CardInt event when abort pulse.

field.name: IO_ENABLE_INT
field.description: This event is set when IO_ENABLE[fn] at FN0 0x02 is transitioned from 0-to-1 that is written by host

field.name: IO_DISABLE_INT
field.description: This event is set when IO_ENABLE[fn] at FN0 0x02 is transitioned from 1-to-0 that is written by host

field.name: CMD_PORT_UPLD_CARD_INT
field.description: This event is set if current cmd53 upload/rx data transfer is completed.

field.name: CMD_PORT_DNLD_CARD_INT
field.description: This event is set if current cmd53 download/tx data transfer is completed.

field.name: CMD52_WR_ERR_INT
field.description: This event is set if host issues cmd52 write access to off-domain register during sleep mode.

field.name: CMD52_RD_ERR_INT
field.description: This event is set if host issues cmd52 read access to off-domain register during sleep mode.

field.name: CMD53_WR_ERR_INT
field.description: This event is set if host issues cmd53 write access to off-domain register during sleep mode.

field.name: CMD53_RD_ERR_INT
field.description: This event is set if host issues cmd53 read access to off-domain register during sleep mode.

field.name: CARD_INT_RSR0
field.description: Card Interrupt Reset Select[7:0] 0 = ISR bit clears when 0 is written to it 1 = ISR bit clears when read

field.name: CARD_INT_RSR1

field.description: APU default interrupt. The purpose of this interrupt is to catch any erroneous host wakeup case. In the event of an erroneous host wakeup, it is possible that the host wakeup interrupt will not assert. In order to ensure that the APU does not get stuck in some unknown state, this dummy interrupt will be thrown in it's place. Firmware should only care about this bit if no other interrupts are set in this register.

field.name: CPU1_DCODE_INV_ADDR_CLR
field.description: After the invalid address int happened on CPU1 dcode bus, the cpu1 will read the ERR ISR and read the bus state which cause the timeout and then set this bit to 1 to clear the CPU1 Dcode invalid addr logic to start recroding next transaction. This is self clearing bit

field.name: CPU1_ICODE_INV_ADDR_CLR
field.description: After the invalid address int happened on CPU1 icode bus, the cpu1 will read the ERR ISR and read the bus state which cause the timeout and then set this bit to 1 to clear the CPU1 Icode invalid addr logic to start recroding next transaction. This is self clearing bit

field.name: CPU1_ACCESS_CTRL
field.description: CPU1 will read CIU_CPU_CPU1_ACCESS_CRTL and set CIU_CPU1_ACCESS_CRTL bit. After writing the bit, the CPU1 will check if the CIU_CPU_CPU1_ACCESS_CRTL bit is set or not. If set then CPU1 will access the resource (for e.g CSU).

field.name: CPU2_ACCESS_CTRL
field.description: CPU2 will read CIU_CPU_CPU2_ACCESS_CRTL and set CIU_CPU2_ACCESS_CRTL bit. After writing the bit, the CPU2 will check if the CIU_CPU_CPU2_ACCESS_CRTL bit is set or not. If set then CPU2 will access the resource (for e.g CSU).

field.name: CPU3_ACCESS_CTRL
field.description: CPU3 will read CIU_CPU_CPU3_ACCESS_CRTL and set CIU_CPU3_ACCESS_CRTL bit. After writing the bit, the CPU3 will check if the CIU_CPU_CPU3_ACCESS_CRTL bit is set or not. If set then CPU3 will access the resource (for e.g CSU).

field.name: FW_DWLD_INFO_VALID
field.description: After writing the bit[8] and bit[16], the CPU1 writes valid bit to indicate to cpu2 that information is valid and ready to use. CPU2 polls this bit and once set take appropriate action based on bit[8] and bit[16]

field.name: PARALLEL_DWLD
field.description: For the parallel mode of FW download, CPU1 assert this bit to provide information to CPU2.

field.name: CPU2_FW_DWLD_DONE
field.description: For the serial mode of FW download, when CPU1 done with FW download for CPU2 also, then it assert this bit. After this CPU2 can jump to it's ITCM to start execution

field.name: CHIP_INIT_DONE
field.description: After the FW is downloaded (serial or parallel), the CPU1 does the chip init and set this bit. It is used later by boot code in case the FW crash happen, then it doesn't need to do chip init again

field.name: CPU1_TO_CPU3_MSG_RDY
field.description: CPU1 Message for CPU3 is ready. This is self clearing bit. The CPU1 writes 1 to indicate that message for CPU3 is ready. This generates an Interrupt to CPU3 via APU. This is old schema and we should use IMU based scheme.

field.name: CPU3_TO_CPU1_MSG_RDY
field.description: CPU3 Message for CPU1 is ready. This is self clearing bit. The CPU3 writes 1 to indicate that message for CPU1 is ready. This generates an Interrupt to CPU1 via APU. This is old schema and we should use IMU based scheme.

field.name: CPU1_TO_CPU3_MSG_PROCESS_DONE
field.description: CPU1 Message for CPU3 has been read by CPU3 and executed. This is self clearing bit. The CPU3 writes 1 to indicate that message sent by CPU1 is executed. This generates an Interrupt to CPU1 via CIU1.

field.name: CPU3_TO_CPU1_MSG_PROCESS_DONE
field.description: CPU3 Message for CPU1 has been read by CPU1 and executed. This is self clearing bit. The CPU1 writes 1 to indicate that message send by CPU3 is executed. This generates an Interrupt to CPU3 via CIU1.

field.name: OTP_SPARE0

field.description: SPARE register for future ECO's, h/w default is 0xFFFF

field.name: OTP_ALL_BITS_EQ_ZERO
field.description: All bits equal to zero (READ ONLY)

field.name: OTP_ADDR
field.description: The otp_addr is composed of Bank select[16:13] and row address[12:7], the address will select a row or a data line of a bank that contains 64 bits of s/w usable data plus the ATE test bit and data line valid bit and the security bit.

field.name: REGULATOR_SV
field.description: Stepdown regulator Rate Control, default = 2'b10 (2'b10==2.6V for 40nm)

field.name: REGULATOR_EN
field.description: Stepdown regulator output enable, only valid if regulator_EN_bypass==1.

field.name: MACRO_RD_DONE
field.description: RD_DONE is from the OTP bank (selected by otp_addr_reg[9:6]).

field.name: MACRO_TEST
field.description: S/W control bits to TEST[3:0] inputs.

field.name: REG_CSTATE_RESET
field.description: Reset OTP ctrl sm (for debugging purpose).

field.name: OTP_PROG_SEQ_CODE_CLK_OTPMEM
field.description: Clock input, used to program the match code into all the OTP memories

field.name: OTP_PROG_SEQ_CODE_OTPMEM
field.description: Data input, used to program the match code into all the OTP memories.

field.name: OTP_PROG_SEQ_CODE_CLK_VTR
field.description: Clock input, used to program the match code into all the VTR (Step Down regulator)

field.name: OTP_PROG_SEQ_CODE_VTR
field.description: Data input, used to program the match code into all the VTR (Step Down regulator)

field.name: OTP_PROG_SEQ_CODE_MUX_SEL
field.description: SELECT OTP register for the match Code programming.

field.name: OTP_FORCE_SCLK_MEM_PROG
field.description: Only used for OTP memory programming: Set this bit to allow the match code programming, clear this bit after the match code programming before start otp memory programming.

field.name: OTP_FORCE_STEPDOWN_PROG
field.description: For OTP memory programming: This bit need to be set before the match code programming and clear this bit after the otp memory contents programming is done.

field.name: OTP_CMD_START
field.description: Write 1 to start otp access command execution and it clears the ctrl_cmd_done bit.

field.name: OTP_CMD
field.description: OTP access commands (the command execution finishes when the ctrl_cmd_done bit is set):

field.name: TPGM_2US
field.description: Specify the width of the programming pulse (in number of pclk cycle), the number depends on the pclk frequency and the pulse width requirement (OTP macro specifies between 2us up to 10us).

field.name: TSQ_MINUS_TRD
field.description: Read data access time, the value to enter is tSQ(70ns)-tRD. The default value is based on 32MHz LSB clock.

field.name: TRD_20NS_LOW
field.description: For 28nm. Read pulse width lower two bits(higher two bits are in OTP_PARAM2_REG[12:11]). The default value is based on 32MHz LSB clock.

field.name: TVHV_OFF_10US
field.description: Specify the VHV turn OFF time before the OTP read access. The default value is based on 32MHz

field.name: TSU_300NS
field.description: Specify setup time for few of the OTP control signals. The default value is based on 32MHz LSB clock.

field.name: TVHV_ON_10US
field.description: Specify the VHV turn ON time before the OTP programming access. The default value is based on 32MHz LSB clock.

field.name: TRD_20NS_HIGH
field.description: For 28nm, Read pulse width higher two bits (lower two bits are in OTP_PARAM0_REG[15:14]). The default value is based on 32MHz LSB clock.

field.name: SET_OTP_BYPASS
field.description: SET OTP bypass mode, all the OTP interface control signals are under register control by s/w.

field.name: SCLK
field.description: Note: Only valid in the OTP BYPASS mode (OTP_BYPASS_MODE_REG[0]=1).

field.name: PGM_B
field.description: Note: Only valid in the OTP BYPASS mode (OTP_BYPASS_MODE_REG[0]=1).

field.name: LOAD
field.description: Note: Only valid in the OTP BYPASS mode (OTP_BYPASS_MODE_REG[0]=1).

field.name: MUX_DOUT
field.description: Note: Only valid in the OTP BYPASS mode (OTP_BYPASS_MODE_REG[0]=1).

field.name: MUX_RD_DONE
field.description: Note: Only valid in the OTP BYPASS mode (OTP_BYPASS_MODE_REG[0]=1).

field.name: BIT_ADDRESS
field.description: Note: Only valid in the OTP BYPASS mode (OTP_BYPASS_MODE_REG[0]=1).

field.name: CSB
field.description: Note: Only valid in the OTP BYPASS mode (OTP_BYPASS_MODE_REG[0]=1).

field.name: OTP_RST_B
field.description: S/W reset bit to RST_B input of each OTP macro

field.name: OTP_POR_B
field.description: S/W por bit to POR_B input of each OTP macro.

field.name: OTP_WRITE_LOCK
field.description: "1 sticky bit, once it is set it will stay at set state until POR_ONLY reset to 0.

field.description: sw reset from CPU for sensor and controller

field.name: ADCC_SW_ENABLE
field.description: sw enable from CPU for sensor and controller

field.name: ADCC_TEST_CAL_BYPASS
field.description: bypass calibration for ATE or other test

field.description: It selects one of the testbuses of ADCC.

field.name: ADCC_ERR_GAIN_BYPASS
field.description: Bypass error gain adjustment in ADCC data output

field.name: ADCC_ERR_GAIN
field.description: IT is 4 bIT signed integer value of error gain of SARADC. If adcc_err_gain_bypass is set as 1, then this value is not considered for error gain adjustment of ADCC data output. Example: If value of this field is 4'b1110, then IT is -2 in decimal.

field.name: ADCC_OFFSET_CODE
field.description: OFFSET of ADC computed after calibration. It is a signed number (2's complement format) with 1 fractional bit. Example, If binary value of this field is 1111_1111_0011 then it represents -6.5 in decimal. Note that, this field is valid only when adcc_cal_done bit is 1.

field.name: INTID
field.description: Interrupt ID of the interrupt to trigger, in the range 0-479.

register.name: AIRCR
register.description: Application Interrupt and Reset Control Register

field.name: VECTCLRACTIVE
field.description: Reserved for Debug use. This bit reads as 0. When writing to the register you must write 0 to this bit, otherwise behavior is UNPREDICTABLE. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: SYSRESETREQ
field.description: System reset request. This bit allows software or a debugger to request a system reset. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW if SYSRESETREQS is 0. When SYSRESETREQS is set to 1, from Non-secure state this bit acts as RAZ/WI.

enumeratedValue.name: NO_REQUEST
enumeratedValue.description: Do not request a system reset.

field.name: SYSRESETREQS
field.description: System reset request, Secure state only. The value of this bit defines whether the SYSRESETREQ bit is functional for Non-secure use. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure State and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is available to both Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_ONLY
enumeratedValue.description: SYSRESETREQ functionality is only available to Secure state.

field.name: PRIGROUP
field.description: Interrupt priority grouping field. This field determines the split of group priority from subpriority. This bit is banked between Security states

field.name: BFHFNMINS
field.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI Non-secure enable. The value of this bit defines whether BusFault and NMI exceptions are Non-secure, and whether exceptions target the Non-secure HardFault exception. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure-state and RO from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: BusFault, HardFault, and NMI are Secure.

enumeratedValue.name: NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: BusFault and NMI are Non-secure and exceptions can target Non-secure HardFault.

field.name: PRIS
field.description: Prioritize Secure exceptions. The value of this bit defines whether Secure exception priority boosting is enabled. This bit is not banked between Security states. RW from Secure state and RAZ/WI from Non-secure state.

enumeratedValue.name: SAME_PRIORITY
enumeratedValue.description: Priority ranges of Secure and Non-secure exceptions are identical

field.name: ENDIANNESS
field.description: Data endianness bit. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: VECTKEY
field.description: Register key: Reads as 0xFA05. On writes, write 0x5FA to VECTKEY, otherwise the write is ignored. This Field is not banked between Security states.

register.name: SCR
register.description: The SCR controls features of entry to and exit from low-power state.

field.name: SLEEPONEXIT
field.description: Indicates sleep-on-exit when returning from Handler mode to Thread mode. Setting this bit to 1 enables an interrupt driven application to avoid returning to an empty main application. This bit is banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: NOT_SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Do not sleep when returning to Thread mode.

enumeratedValue.name: SLEEP
enumeratedValue.description: Enter sleep, or deep sleep, on return from an ISR

field.name: SLEEPDEEP
field.description: Controls whether the processor uses sleep or deep sleep as its low-power mode. This bit is not banked between Security states.

field.name: SLEEPDEEPS
field.description: Controls whether the SLEEPDEEP bit is only accessible from the Secure state. This bit in only accessible from the Secure state, and behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Nonsecure state. This bit is not banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_AND_NON_SECURE
enumeratedValue.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit is accessible from both Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURE_ONLY
enumeratedValue.description: The SLEEPDEEP bit behaves as RAZ/WI when accessed from the Non-secure state.

field.name: SEVONPEND
field.description: Send Event on Pending bit. When an event or interrupt enters pending state, the event signal wakes up the processor from WFE. If the processor is not waiting for an event, the event is registered and affects the next WFE. The processor also wakes up on execution of an SEV instruction or an external event. This bit is banked between Security states.

enumeratedValue.name: EXCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
enumeratedValue.description: Only enabled interrupts or events can wakeup the processor, disabled interrupts are excluded.

enumeratedValue.name: INCLUDE_DISABLED_INTERRUPTS
enumeratedValue.description: Enabled events and all interrupts, including disabled interrupts, can wakeup the processor

register.name: SHCSR
register.description: System Handler Control and State Register

enumeratedValue.description: Debug monitor exception is not active.

field.name: ENABLE
field.description: Enable. Enables the SAU. This bit is RAZ/WI when the Security Extension is implemented without an SAU region.

enumeratedValue.name: SECURED_MEMORY
enumeratedValue.description: Memory is marked as Secure and is not Non-secure callable.

field.name: SREGION
field.description: SAU regions. The number of implemented SAU regions.

register.name: RNR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Number Register

register.name: RBAR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Base Address Register

field.name: BADDR
field.description: Base address. Holds bits[31:5] of the base address for the selected SAU region. Bits[4:0] of the base address are defined as 0x00.

register.name: RLAR
register.description: Security Attribution Unit Region Limit Address Register

field.name: NSC
field.description: Non-secure callable. Controls whether Non-secure state is permitted to execute an SG instruction from this region.

field.name: LADDR
field.description: Limit address. Holds bits[31:5] of the limit address for the selected SAU region. Bits[4:0] of the limit address are defined as 0x1F.

field.name: ADDRESS
field.description: When the SFARVALID bit of the SFSR is set to 1, this field holds the address of an access that caused an SAU violation.
